headline: Bet the company on one enterprise deal
body: A Fortune 500 company wants a custom version of your product. Your team estimates six months and real money to build it. Land it and you're in the door at a company a thousand times your size. Miss and you've spent both on nothing.

options.label: Build it and go all in
options.detail: Commit the team and the cash now, before you know if they'll actually sign.

gamble.winText: Deal closed. You're in the big leagues.
gamble.loseText: Deal fell through. Six months wasted, most of the bank gone.

options.storyHeadline: Made a major enterprise bet

options.label: Stick to your roadmap
options.detail: Let the deal go. Whatever you're already building stays the priority.
options.storyHeadline: Decided not to swing for the fences

headline: A strategic buyer wants to acquire you
body: It's a real, fully-priced offer for the whole company. Your team thinks you could be worth far more if you stay independent another few years. The buyer's CEO is on the call right now, waiting for an answer.

options.label: Take the offer
options.detail: Sign today, at today's price, and end the company on this note.
options.storyHeadline: Sold the company to a strategic buyer

options.label: Decline, hold out for more
options.detail: Turn it down and bet that staying independent is worth more later.

gamble.winText: You were right. Your valuation roughly doubled.
gamble.loseText: The market shifted and the buyer moved on. You're back to bootstrapping, offer gone.

options.storyHeadline: Rejected an acquisition offer

headline: Pivot to a new market
body: A related market looks ten times bigger than the one you're in. Chasing it means abandoning your current customers and starting from scratch.

options.label: Drop everything and chase it
options.detail: Walk away from today's customers and rebuild for the bigger market.

gamble.winText: New market is 10x bigger. You nailed it.
gamble.loseText: New market doesn't want it. Lost original market too.

options.storyHeadline: Pivoted to new market

options.label: Stay the course
options.detail: Let the bigger market go and keep serving the customers you already have.
options.storyHeadline: Stayed focused on the core market

headline: The last pitch
body: One investor left on the list. {INVESTOR} sees eleven companies a week and remembers two.

options.label: Fly there tonight and pitch in person
options.detail: Everything, on one meeting.
options.storyHeadline: Flew across the world for one last pitch

gamble.winText: They wrote the cheque on the spot.
gamble.loseText: You spent your last savings on flights and heard nothing.

options.label: Cut half the staff and stop needing the money
options.detail: Runway stretches. Morale takes the hit.
options.storyHeadline: Cut deep instead of chasing one last cheque

headline: All of it on one customer
body: A company forty times your size will decide in one meeting. Preparing properly means dropping everything else for three months.

options.label: Drop everything and go for it
options.detail: Win big, or lose a quarter of the business.
options.storyHeadline: Dropped everything to chase one enormous customer

gamble.winText: You won, and they became most of your revenue.
gamble.loseText: They chose someone else. You lost a quarter of the business preparing.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Landed the deal that changed the company
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Lost everything preparing for one deal

options.label: Prepare in the evenings, keep the lights on
options.detail: A much smaller shot, nothing lost either way.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the day job while chasing a big deal quietly

headline: Move the money
body: Everyone says the currency will fall. Everyone has said that for two years.

options.label: Move every cent into dollars this week
options.detail: A real bet on your own timing.
options.storyHeadline: Bet the treasury on a currency call

gamble.winText: The currency fell 40%. You saw it coming.
gamble.loseText: It strengthened instead. The transfer fees and the swing cost you a fifth.

options.label: Move half
options.detail: Safe. Boring. Usually correct.
options.storyHeadline: Hedged the currency bet

headline: Burn it down and start again
body: Your engineers say the product is held together with tape. Rebuilding takes eight months of shipping nothing.

options.label: Rebuild it
options.detail: Faster than anyone in the market, or fourteen months and nothing to show.
options.storyHeadline: Rebuilt the product from the ground up

gamble.winText: You emerged faster than anyone in the market.
gamble.loseText: It took fourteen months. It wasn't better. Customers left.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: The rebuild put you years ahead
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: The rebuild cost more than it gave back

options.label: Patch it forever
options.detail: Nothing breaks today. Everything is slower every year.
options.storyHeadline: Kept patching instead of rebuilding

headline: Ship it Friday
body: It's nearly ready. The press embargo lifts Monday. Your lead engineer says one more week.

options.label: Ship Friday
options.detail: Catch the news cycle, or break in public on the biggest day you'll ever have.
options.storyHeadline: Shipped early to catch a press window

gamble.winText: You caught the news cycle perfectly.
gamble.loseText: It broke in public on the biggest day you'll ever have.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Shipped early and landed everywhere at once
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Shipped early and broke in public

options.label: Delay a week and miss the coverage
options.detail: Safe. Nobody notices you launched.
options.storyHeadline: Delayed the launch and missed the coverage

headline: The famous boss
body: A well-known executive wants to run your company day-to-day.

options.label: Hire them
options.detail: They could double the business, or gut it before they leave.
options.storyHeadline: Handed the company to a famous outside executive

gamble.winText: They doubled the business in three years.
gamble.loseText: They alienated your best people and the investors, then left after a year.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: The famous hire doubled the business
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: The famous hire nearly sank the business

options.label: Keep doing it yourself
options.detail: Absolute control. Personally exhausting.
options.storyHeadline: Kept running the company yourself

headline: The enormous advert
body: One advert, one night, in front of an audience of millions. It costs nearly everything you have.

options.label: Buy the slot
options.detail: Wake up famous, or wake up having spent it all on nothing.
options.storyHeadline: Bought a once-in-a-career advertising slot

gamble.winStoryHeadline: One advert made the company famous overnight
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: One enormous advert vanished without a trace

options.label: Spend a tenth of it on small ads that definitely work
options.detail: Nobody ever tells this story. It works anyway.
options.storyHeadline: Spent small and steady instead of going big

headline: Sue the giant
body: A company two thousand times your size took your idea wholesale. Your lawyer thinks you have a case.

options.label: Sue them
options.detail: A settlement that makes headlines, or years of bills and a loss.
options.storyHeadline: Sued a company vastly bigger than yours

gamble.winText: They settled rather than be embarrassed.
gamble.loseText: Four years of legal bills, and you lost.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Won a settlement from a giant
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Lost a long legal fight with a giant

options.label: Let it go and move faster than them
options.detail: The sensible option, which is why nobody picks it.
options.storyHeadline: Let a bigger rival's theft go and outran them instead

headline: Tell the truth first
body: Something went wrong. Nobody outside the company knows yet. You could fix it quietly.

options.label: Publish everything before anyone asks
options.detail: Praised for a decade, or the reason there's a story at all.
options.storyHeadline: Published a mistake before anyone found out

gamble.winText: You're praised for a decade. It becomes the thing people know about you.
gamble.loseText: It became a news story that would otherwise never have existed.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Went public with a mistake and earned trust
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Went public with a mistake and made it a story

options.label: Fix it quietly
options.detail: Usually fine. Sometimes much worse later.
options.storyHeadline: Fixed a mistake quietly instead of going public

headline: Open the second country
body: Everyone says go now. Everyone also said that to companies that died doing it.

options.label: Go all in — office, staff, everything
options.detail: Double the business, or eighteen months learning the market is different.
options.storyHeadline: Went all in opening a second country

gamble.winText: It worked, and doubled the business.
gamble.loseText: Eighteen months and a real amount of cash later, you retreated.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: The second country doubled the business
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: The second country was an expensive lesson

options.label: Sell there from home first, no office
options.detail: Slow, cheap, usually correct.
options.storyHeadline: Tested a second country remotely first

headline: Go on the television show
body: The one where people pitch to rich investors on camera. Twelve million viewers. No editing rights.

options.label: Go on
options.detail: An offer live on air, or taken apart on national television.
options.storyHeadline: Went on national television to pitch

gamble.winText: You got an offer live, and the phone didn't stop for a month.
gamble.loseText: They took you apart on national television. The clip lives forever.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: The television pitch landed a deal live on air
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: The television pitch went badly, on camera, forever

options.label: Don't
options.detail: Safe. {RIVAL} goes on instead, and it works for them.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down the television pitch show

headline: Poach the whole team
body: Six engineers at {RIVAL} would come over together if you asked. All six or none.

options.label: Take all six
options.detail: Triple your output, or import a faction that breaks your culture.
options.storyHeadline: Poached a rival's entire engineering team at once

gamble.loseText: They arrived as a bloc and ran things their way. Your original team left.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Poaching a rival's whole team paid off
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Poaching a rival's whole team broke the culture

options.label: Take the best two
options.detail: Quiet, real gains, no drama.
options.storyHeadline: Hired just the best two off a rival's team

headline: Rename the company
body: The name has never worked. Changing it costs a fortune and everybody who knows you knows the old one.

options.label: Change it
options.detail: A name that finally fits, or a very expensive confusion.
options.storyHeadline: Renamed the company entirely

gamble.winText: The new name fits so well nobody remembers the old one within two years.
gamble.loseText: You confused every customer you had.

options.label: Keep it and stop worrying
options.detail: Free. Imperfect. Fine.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the name that never quite worked
